newsitem.title: UK: New rift for British royals over blood sports.
newsitem.headline: New rift for British royals over blood sports.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana, already at war with Prince Charles, is now fighting with her son William over his lust for blood sports, the Sunday Mirror reported.
"Diana: My fear for gun-crazed Wills" the paper said in a front-page story detailing a new rift inside the royal family.
It said Diana feared her eldest son would turn into "a remorseless hunter with a blood-lust" after his first kill.
"The animal-loving princess is deeply concerned about the psychological effects that hunting -- so favoured by the royals -- will have on pricess William and Harry," it said.

William is believed to have stalked and shot his first stag last month on Queen Elizabeth's Balmoral estate in the Scottish Highlands. The 14-year-old prince reportedly made the kill in the company of his 12-year-old brother Harry and Prince Charles.
After the kill, the stag would have been "gralloched", or disembowelled, in order to prevent the carcass from bloating and to make it easier to drag down the hill.
Charles is a keen hunter, as is Tiggy Legge-Bourke, the aide who looks after the boys when they are with their father.
Legge-Bourke has even helped the princes practise their marksmanship by shooting rabbits and crows but Diana, who was divorced from Charles in August, abhors blood sports.
"In a stern warning from the palace, the princess has been told that their pastime is none of her business and she must not speak out," said the paper.
"She has told her son she could not stop him hunting -- but she did not want to know the grisly details," said the Mirror. Diana has reportedly banned all talk of hunting in her presence.
But William is so keen on the family sport that he may get his own shotgun for Christmas, said the paper. He has also reportedly chosen to spend New Year shooting rather than skiing.

"William is hooked on hunting in a big way and there is nothing Diana can do to stop him," the paper quoted an insider as saying. "She thinks the world of her sons but she finds it difficult to stomach the gruesome details of their latest hobby."
